tool.name: Create View
tool.description: Create a new generative view from a USE JSON document. The view becomes visible in Create > Views and renders as real SwiftUI.

document.description: USE document. Either a bare root spec {"component": "vstack", "props": {...}, "children": [...]} or, for views with logic, {"operations": [<executor ops run once at load>], "root": {<spec>}}

ai.systemPromptSection:
### create_view
Create a generative view from a USE JSON document. Call get_view_catalog first to learn valid components, modifiers, actions, and operations.

**Two document shapes:**
1. Bare root spec: `{"component":"vstack","props":{...},"children":[...]}`
2. With logic: `{"operations":[<executor ops>],"root":{<spec>}}` — operations run ONCE at view load (define functions, seed state with set); buttons then trigger them with `{"type":"call","name":...}` actions.

**Format:**
```tool_request
{"tool":"create_view","query":"{\"name\":\"Counter\",\"document\":{\"component\":\"vstack\",\"props\":{\"spacing\":16},\"children\":[{\"component\":\"text\",\"props\":{\"content\":\"Hello\"}}]}}"}
```

Key patterns: ForEach repeats its FIRST child as a template (items = inline array or '$stateKey'; use $item / $index / $item.path inside). For sheets/alerts use the sheet/alert MODIFIER props with an isPresented state key toggled by a button — NOT the sheet/alert actions. The document is validated before saving; on failure you get actionable errors.

usageExamples.description: Sheet via modifier (preferred over sheet action)
